evidence: Route 9 (response-frequency matching), used to check the one step the file's own labels do not cover: data/dpt_noncognitive_traits.py's rename of source column Q15_k to IRW code iri_N. Counted every item x resp cell in the source xlsx columns 16-30 (labelled IR_Index_1..IR_Index_26 in row 2, rows 5-302) against table(item, resp) on the live IRW table: 74 non-empty cells compared, 0 mismatched. Examples: iri_1 source 5/45/76/116/56 vs live 5/45/76/116/56; iri_12 103/125/40/25/5 vs 103/125/40/25/5; iri_21 1/18/45/148/86 vs 1/18/45/148/86; iri_8 has no resp=1 in either (18/40/153/87 vs 18/40/153/87), which also explains the live resp_min of 2 for that item alone. The 15 frequency profiles are mutually distinct, so any permutation of the 15 columns would break at least one cell; this therefore distinguishes every item from every other item and ties each to the row-4 wording shipped for it. What it does NOT establish: the option anchors. resp 1 = 'does not describe me well' and resp 5 = 'describes me very well' come from the paper's Methods (which states 0-4 while the data store 1-5) plus item content, not from these counts.
